sp-leeds-manutd: Manchester United were held to a 1-1 draw by Leeds at Elland Road on Sunday.
Bryan Mbeumo put United ahead in the 35th minute, tapping in a cross from Youri Tielemans. But a corner wasn’t cleared, and Dominic Calvert-Lewin equalised from close range in the 51st minute.

According to Yahoo Sports, United now have one win from seven league games. That’s their fewest at this stage of a top-flight season since 1986-87. Al Jazeera reported they’re 13th, with Leeds seventh.
Michael Carrick acknowledged the situation did not look good, but said he was confident his side could go on a good run.
biz-ftse-falls: London’s FTSE 100 fell 1.1% on Monday, to 10,764.69, ending three straight sessions of gains.
Miners were among the biggest drags as copper prices dipped. Anglo American lost 4.1%, and Glencore 3.3%. Barclays also fell sharply, after a report of Bank of England scrutiny.

Serica Energy fell 2.6% after flagging a further delay to restarting its Triton vessel. On the way up, Pets at Home rose about 6.7% after a broker upgrade, and Mulberry gained after reporting higher sales.
The FTSE 250 slipped 0.6%, ending a six-day winning run. Across Europe, shares opened lower as France counted the cost of weekend riots.
UK jobs data is due on Tuesday, and inflation figures on Wednesday.
